# `vidar:sched`

The public procs and types of `import "vidar:sched"`: goroutines, channels, `select`, locks and I/O that parks only the goroutine. Chapter 14, [Goroutines and Channels](ch14-00-goroutines.md), explains how they behave.

> **Goroutines are disabled for now.** Importing `vidar:sched` is a compile error unless `VIDAR_GOROUTINES=1` is set in the environment. The examples here are compiled, but not run.

| Name | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`yield`](#yield) | Lets the other runnable goroutines run before this one continues. |
| [`go`](#go) | Runs the closure on a new goroutine, with the caller's context. |
| [`blocking`](#blocking) | Runs task on a worker thread and parks this goroutine until it returns; the other goroutines keep running. |
| [`sleep`](#sleep) | Parks the calling goroutine for at least `d`; the others keep running. |
| [`after`](#after) | A channel that receives true once d has passed, for select timeouts. |
| [`listen_tcp`](#listen_tcp) | Opens a TCP socket listening on `endpoint`; port 0 picks a free one. |
| [`accept`](#accept) | Waits for the next connection on a listening socket, parking only this goroutine. |
| [`dial`](#dial) | Connects to `endpoint`, parking only this goroutine. |
| [`socket_recv`](#socket_recv) | Receives from a TCP socket into `buf`; with `all`, keeps going until `buf` is full. |
| [`socket_send`](#socket_send) | Sends `buf` on a TCP socket. |
| [`socket_close`](#socket_close) | Closes a TCP socket. |
| [`send_file`](#send_file) | Sends nbytes of file (all of it by default) over the socket, without copying it through user space. |
| [`wait_ready`](#wait_ready) | Waits until the socket can be read from (.Receive) or written to (.Send) without blocking. |
| [`udp_socket`](#udp_socket) | ```vidar main :: proc() { 	sock, err := sched.udp_socket() 	fmt.println(err == nil) 	sched.close(sock) } ```  ```output true ``` |
| [`bind`](#bind) | ```vidar main :: proc() { 	sock, _ := sched.udp_socket() 	defer sched.close(sock) 	err := sched.bind(sock, {net.IP4_Loopback, 0}) 	fmt.println(err == nil) } ```  ```output true ``` |
| [`send_to`](#send_to) | ```vidar ping :: proc(to: net.Endpoint) { 	sock, _ := sched.udp_socket() 	defer sched.close(sock) 	sched.send_to(sock, transmute([]byte)string("ping"), to) } ``` |
| [`recv_from`](#recv_from) | ```vidar echo_once :: proc(sock: net.UDP_Socket) { 	buf: [512]byte 	n, from, err := sched.recv_from(sock, buf[:]) 	if err != nil do return 	sched.send_to(sock, buf[:n], from) } ``` |
| [`udp_close`](#udp_close) | Closes a UDP socket. |
| [`resolve`](#resolve) | ```vidar main :: proc() { 	ep4, _, err := sched.resolve("localhost:8080") 	fmt.println(err == nil, ep4.port) } ```  ```output true 8080 ``` |
| [`File`](#file) | ```vidar size_of_file :: proc(path: string) -> i64 { 	f: sched.File 	err: nbio.FS_Error 	f, err = sched.open(path) 	if err != nil do return -1 	defer sched.close(f) 	_, size, _ := sched.stat(f) 	return size } ``` |
| [`open`](#open) | ```vidar main :: proc() { 	path := "/tmp/vidar-open-example.txt" 	sched.write_entire_file(path, transmute([]byte)string("hello")) 	f, err := sched.open(path)                     // {.Read} by default 	defer sched.close(f) 	fmt.println(err) } ```  ```output None ``` |
| [`read_at`](#read_at) | Reads at offset (the file position is not used); with all, keeps reading until buf is full or the file ends. |
| [`write_at`](#write_at) | ```vidar main :: proc() { 	path := "/tmp/vidar-write-at-example.txt" 	f, _ := sched.open(path, {.Read, .Write, .Create, .Trunc}) 	defer sched.close(f) 	sched.write_at(f, 0, transmute([]byte)string("vidar")) 	_, size, _ := sched.stat(f) 	fmt.println(size) } ```  ```output 5 ``` |
| [`stat`](#stat) | ```vidar main :: proc() { 	path := "/tmp/vidar-stat-example.txt" 	sched.write_entire_file(path, transmute([]byte)string("12345678")) 	f, _ := sched.open(path) 	defer sched.close(f) 	kind, size, _ := sched.stat(f) 	fmt.println(kind, size) } ```  ```output Regular 8 ``` |
| [`file_close`](#file_close) | Closes a file. |
| [`read_entire_file`](#read_entire_file) | ```vidar main :: proc() { 	path := "/tmp/vidar-read-example.txt" 	sched.write_entire_file(path, transmute([]byte)string("line one\n")) 	data, err := sched.read_entire_file(path) 	defer delete(data) 	fmt.print(err, string(data)) } ```  ```output None line one ``` |
| [`write_entire_file`](#write_entire_file) | ```vidar main :: proc() { 	err := sched.write_entire_file("/tmp/vidar-write-example.txt", transmute([]byte)string("saved\n")) 	fmt.println(err) } ```  ```output None ``` |
| [`send`](#send) | A proc group: `chan_send` for a channel, `socket_send` for a TCP socket. |
| [`recv`](#recv) | A proc group: `chan_recv` for a channel, `socket_recv` for a TCP socket. |
| [`close`](#close) | A proc group: `chan_close`, `socket_close`, `udp_close` or `file_close`, by the argument's type. |
| [`Mutex`](#mutex) | ```vidar main :: proc() { 	mu: sched.Mutex 	wg: sched.Wait_Group 	count := 0 	for _ in 0..<3 { 		sched.add(&wg) 		sched.go(proc[&mu, &wg, &count]() { 			defer sched.done(&wg) 			sched.lock(&mu) 			defer sched.unlock(&mu) 			sched.sleep(time.Millisecond)     // held across a park: fine with sched.Mutex 			count += 1 		}) 	} 	sched.wait(&wg) 	fmt.println(count) } ```  ```output 3 ``` |
| [`lock`](#lock) | Parking after the guard is released is safe: a wakeup that comes first queues the goroutine on its thread, where park picks it again, and no other thread takes it until it has switched away. |
| [`unlock`](#unlock) | Hands the lock straight to the longest waiter, if any. |
| [`try_lock`](#try_lock) | ```vidar main :: proc() { 	mu: sched.Mutex 	fmt.println(sched.try_lock(&mu))      // took it 	fmt.println(sched.try_lock(&mu))      // already held 	sched.unlock(&mu) } ```  ```output true false ``` |
| [`Chan`](#chan) | A channel is a handle: copies share one queue. |
| [`make_chan`](#make_chan) | ```vidar main :: proc() { 	unbuffered := sched.make_chan(int) 	buffered := sched.make_chan(string, 8) 	fmt.println(sched.chan_cap(unbuffered), sched.chan_cap(buffered)) } ```  ```output 0 8 ``` |
| [`chan_send`](#chan_send) | Blocks until a receiver takes v, or until there is room in the buffer. |
| [`chan_recv`](#chan_recv) | Blocks until a value arrives; ok is false once the channel is closed and drained. |
| [`chan_close`](#chan_close) | Usually called as `sched.close(ch)`. |
| [`chan_len`](#chan_len) | ```vidar main :: proc() { 	ch := sched.make_chan(int, 4) 	sched.send(ch, 1) 	sched.send(ch, 2) 	fmt.println(sched.chan_len(ch)) } ```  ```output 2 ``` |
| [`chan_cap`](#chan_cap) | ```vidar main :: proc() { 	fmt.println(sched.chan_cap(sched.make_chan(int, 16))) } ```  ```output 16 ``` |
| [`Select_Case`](#select_case) | What `on_recv` and `on_send` make, for `select`:  ```vidar main :: proc() { 	a := sched.make_chan(int, 1) 	b := sched.make_chan(int, 1) 	sched.send(b, 2) 	v: int 	cases := []sched.Select_Case{sched.on_recv(a, &v), sched.on_recv(b, &v)} 	fmt.println(sched.select(..cases), v) } ```  ```output 1 2 ``` |
| [`on_recv`](#on_recv) | A receive for select: the value goes to out^ and whether it arrived (not closed) to ok^; both are optional. |
| [`on_send`](#on_send) | A send of v for select. |
| [`select`](#select) | Waits until one case can proceed, runs it and returns its index. |
| [`try_select`](#try_select) | Like select, but returns -1 at once when no case is ready. |
| [`Wait_Group`](#wait_group) | ```vidar main :: proc() { 	wg: sched.Wait_Group 	for i in 0..<3 { 		sched.add(&wg) 		sched.go(proc[i, &wg]() { 			defer sched.done(&wg) 			sched.sleep(time.Duration(i) * time.Millisecond) 		}) 	} 	sched.wait(&wg) 	fmt.println("all done") } ```  ```output all done ``` |
| [`add`](#add) | ```vidar main :: proc() { 	wg: sched.Wait_Group 	sched.add(&wg, 2)                 // two goroutines to wait for 	sched.go(proc[&wg]() { sched.done(&wg) }) 	sched.go(proc[&wg]() { sched.done(&wg) }) 	sched.wait(&wg) 	fmt.println("both finished") } ```  ```output both finished ``` |
| [`done`](#done) | ```vidar main :: proc() { 	wg: sched.Wait_Group 	sched.add(&wg) 	sched.go(proc[&wg]() { 		defer sched.done(&wg)            // on every path out 		fmt.println("working") 	}) 	sched.wait(&wg) } ```  ```output working ``` |
| [`wait`](#wait) | ```vidar main :: proc() { 	wg: sched.Wait_Group 	sched.wait(&wg)                       // nothing added: returns at once 	fmt.println("nothing to wait for") } ```  ```output nothing to wait for ``` |

## `yield`

```odin
yield :: proc()
```

Lets the other runnable goroutines run before this one continues.

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	sched.go(proc[]() { fmt.println("the other goroutine runs") })
	sched.yield()                    // let it run before main continues
	fmt.println("main continues")
}
```

```output
the other goroutine runs
main continues
```

## `go`

```odin
go :: proc(task: closure(), loc := #caller_location)
```

Runs the closure on a new goroutine, with the caller's context.

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	done := sched.make_chan(string)
	name := "worker"
	sched.go(proc[name, done]() { sched.send(done, fmt.aprintf("%s finished", name)) })
	fmt.println(sched.recv(done))
}
```

```output
worker finished
```

## `blocking`

```odin
blocking :: proc(task: closure(), loc := #caller_location)
```

Runs task on a worker thread and parks this goroutine until it returns; the other goroutines keep running. Use it for calls that block the thread: DNS, C libraries, anything without a sched version. The task runs on another thread, so it must not touch goroutine state without synchronizing.

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	answer := 0
	sched.blocking(proc[&answer]() {
		time.sleep(5 * time.Millisecond)     // would block the scheduler's thread
		answer = 42
	})
	fmt.println(answer)
}
```

```output
42
```

## `sleep`

```odin
sleep :: proc(d: time.Duration, loc := #caller_location)
```

Parks the calling goroutine for at least `d`; the others keep running.

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	sched.go(proc[]() { fmt.println("runs while main sleeps") })
	sched.sleep(10 * time.Millisecond)
	fmt.println("main woke up")
}
```

```output
runs while main sleeps
main woke up
```

## `after`

```odin
after :: proc(d: time.Duration, loc := #caller_location) -> Chan(bool)
```

A channel that receives true once d has passed, for select timeouts.

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	never := sched.make_chan(int)
	switch sched.select(sched.on_recv(never), sched.on_recv(sched.after(10 * time.Millisecond))) {
	case 0: fmt.println("got a value")
	case 1: fmt.println("timed out")
	}
}
```

```output
timed out
```

## `listen_tcp`

```odin
listen_tcp :: proc(endpoint: nbio.Endpoint, backlog := 1000) -> (nbio.TCP_Socket, nbio.Network_Error)
```

Opens a TCP socket listening on `endpoint`; port 0 picks a free one.

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	listener, err := sched.listen_tcp({net.IP4_Loopback, 0})
	if err != nil {
		fmt.println("listen failed:", err)
		return
	}
	defer sched.close(listener)
	ep, _ := net.bound_endpoint(listener)
	fmt.println("listening:", ep.port != 0)
}
```

```output
listening: true
```

## `accept`

```odin
accept :: proc(socket: nbio.TCP_Socket, timeout := nbio.NO_TIMEOUT, loc := #caller_location) -> (nbio.TCP_Socket, nbio.Endpoint, nbio.Accept_Error)
```

Waits for the next connection on a listening socket, parking only this goroutine.

```vidar
serve :: proc(listener: net.TCP_Socket) {
	for {
		client, from, err := sched.accept(listener)
		if err != nil do return
		fmt.println("connection from", from)
		sched.go(proc[client]() { sched.close(client) })
	}
}
```

## `dial`

```odin
dial :: proc(endpoint: nbio.Endpoint, timeout := nbio.NO_TIMEOUT, loc := #caller_location) -> (nbio.TCP_Socket, nbio.Network_Error)
```

Connects to `endpoint`, parking only this goroutine.

```vidar
fetch_banner :: proc(ep: net.Endpoint) -> string {
	conn, err := sched.dial(ep, timeout = 2 * time.Second)
	if err != nil do return ""
	defer sched.close(conn)
	buf: [128]byte
	n, _ := sched.recv(conn, buf[:])
	return strings.clone(string(buf[:n]))
}
```

## `socket_recv`

```odin
socket_recv :: proc(socket: nbio.TCP_Socket, buf: []byte, all := false, timeout := nbio.NO_TIMEOUT, loc := #caller_location) -> (int, nbio.Recv_Error)
```

Receives from a TCP socket into `buf`; with `all`, keeps going until `buf` is full. Usually called as `sched.recv(socket, buf)`.

```vidar
read_exact :: proc(conn: net.TCP_Socket, buf: []byte) -> bool {
	n, err := sched.socket_recv(conn, buf, all = true)
	return err == nil && n == len(buf)
}
```

## `socket_send`

```odin
socket_send :: proc(socket: nbio.TCP_Socket, buf: []byte, timeout := nbio.NO_TIMEOUT, loc := #caller_location) -> (int, nbio.Send_Error)
```

Sends `buf` on a TCP socket. Usually called as `sched.send(socket, buf)`.

```vidar
say :: proc(conn: net.TCP_Socket, msg: string) -> bool {
	_, err := sched.socket_send(conn, transmute([]byte)msg)
	return err == nil
}
```

## `socket_close`

```odin
socket_close :: proc(socket: nbio.TCP_Socket, loc := #caller_location)
```

Closes a TCP socket. Usually called as `sched.close(socket)`.

```vidar
hang_up :: proc(conn: net.TCP_Socket) {
	sched.socket_close(conn)
}
```

## `send_file`

```odin
send_file :: proc(socket: nbio.TCP_Socket, file: File, offset := 0, nbytes := nbio.SEND_ENTIRE_FILE, timeout := nbio.NO_TIMEOUT, loc := #caller_location) -> (int, nbio.Send_File_Error)
```

Sends nbytes of file (all of it by default) over the socket, without copying it through user space.

```vidar
serve_file :: proc(conn: net.TCP_Socket, path: string) {
	f, err := sched.open(path)
	if err != nil do return
	defer sched.close(f)
	sched.send_file(conn, f)          // the whole file, without copying it through memory
}
```

## `wait_ready`

```odin
wait_ready :: proc(socket: nbio.Any_Socket, event: nbio.Poll_Event, timeout := nbio.NO_TIMEOUT, loc := #caller_location) -> nbio.Poll_Result
```

Waits until the socket can be read from (.Receive) or written to (.Send) without blocking.

```vidar
wait_for_input :: proc(conn: net.TCP_Socket) -> bool {
	return sched.wait_ready(conn, .Receive, timeout = time.Second) == .Ready
}
```

## `Mutex`

```odin
Mutex :: struct
```

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	mu: sched.Mutex
	wg: sched.Wait_Group
	count := 0
	for _ in 0..<3 {
		sched.add(&wg)
		sched.go(proc[&mu, &wg, &count]() {
			defer sched.done(&wg)
			sched.lock(&mu)
			defer sched.unlock(&mu)
			sched.sleep(time.Millisecond)     // held across a park: fine with sched.Mutex
			count += 1
		})
	}
	sched.wait(&wg)
	fmt.println(count)
}
```

```output
3
```

## `lock`

```odin
lock :: proc(m: ^Mutex, loc := #caller_location)
```

Parking after the guard is released is safe: a wakeup that comes first queues the goroutine on its thread, where park picks it again, and no other thread takes it until it has switched away.

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	mu: sched.Mutex
	sched.lock(&mu)
	fmt.println("holding the lock")
	sched.unlock(&mu)
}
```

```output
holding the lock
```

## `unlock`

```odin
unlock :: proc(m: ^Mutex)
```

Hands the lock straight to the longest waiter, if any.

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	mu: sched.Mutex
	sched.lock(&mu)
	sched.unlock(&mu)
	fmt.println(sched.try_lock(&mu))      // free again
	sched.unlock(&mu)
}
```

```output
true
```

## `try_lock`

```odin
try_lock :: proc(m: ^Mutex) -> bool
```

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	mu: sched.Mutex
	fmt.println(sched.try_lock(&mu))      // took it
	fmt.println(sched.try_lock(&mu))      // already held
	sched.unlock(&mu)
}
```

```output
true
false
```

## `Chan`

```odin
Chan :: struct($T: typeid)
```

A channel is a handle: copies share one queue. The zero Chan is nil and blocks forever.

```vidar
producer :: proc(out: sched.Chan(int)) {
	for i in 1..=3 do sched.send(out, i)
	sched.close(out)
}

main :: proc() {
	ch := sched.make_chan(int)
	sched.go(proc[ch]() { producer(ch) })
	for {
		v := sched.recv(ch) or_break
		fmt.print(v, "")
	}
	fmt.println()
}
```

```output
1 2 3
```

## `make_chan`

```odin
make_chan :: proc($T: typeid, capacity := 0) -> Chan(T)
```

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	unbuffered := sched.make_chan(int)
	buffered := sched.make_chan(string, 8)
	fmt.println(sched.chan_cap(unbuffered), sched.chan_cap(buffered))
}
```

```output
0 8
```

## `chan_send`

```odin
chan_send :: proc(c: Chan($T), v: T, loc := #caller_location)
```

Blocks until a receiver takes v, or until there is room in the buffer.

Usually called as `sched.send(ch, v)`.

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	ch := sched.make_chan(int, 2)
	sched.chan_send(ch, 1)
	sched.chan_send(ch, 2)
	fmt.println(sched.chan_len(ch))
}
```

```output
2
```

## `chan_recv`

```odin
chan_recv :: proc(c: Chan($T), loc := #caller_location) -> (v: T, ok: bool) #optional_ok
```

Blocks until a value arrives; ok is false once the channel is closed and drained.

Usually called as `sched.recv(ch)`. `ok` is false once the channel is closed and empty.

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	ch := sched.make_chan(int, 1)
	sched.send(ch, 5)
	sched.close(ch)
	a, ok1 := sched.chan_recv(ch)
	b, ok2 := sched.chan_recv(ch)
	fmt.println(a, ok1, b, ok2)
}
```

```output
5 true 0 false
```

## `chan_close`

```odin
chan_close :: proc(c: Chan($T))
```

Usually called as `sched.close(ch)`.

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	ch := sched.make_chan(int)
	sched.chan_close(ch)
	_, ok := sched.recv(ch)
	fmt.println(ok)
}
```

```output
false
```

## `chan_len`

```odin
chan_len :: proc(c: Chan($T)) -> int
```

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	ch := sched.make_chan(int, 4)
	sched.send(ch, 1)
	sched.send(ch, 2)
	fmt.println(sched.chan_len(ch))
}
```

```output
2
```

## `chan_cap`

```odin
chan_cap :: proc(c: Chan($T)) -> int
```

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	fmt.println(sched.chan_cap(sched.make_chan(int, 16)))
}
```

```output
16
```

## `Select_Case`

```odin
Select_Case :: struct
```

What `on_recv` and `on_send` make, for `select`:

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	a := sched.make_chan(int, 1)
	b := sched.make_chan(int, 1)
	sched.send(b, 2)
	v: int
	cases := []sched.Select_Case{sched.on_recv(a, &v), sched.on_recv(b, &v)}
	fmt.println(sched.select(..cases), v)
}
```

```output
1 2
```

## `on_recv`

```odin
on_recv :: proc(c: Chan($T), out: ^T = nil, ok: ^bool = nil) -> Select_Case
```

A receive for select: the value goes to out^ and whether it arrived (not closed) to ok^; both are optional.

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	ch := sched.make_chan(int, 1)
	sched.close(ch)
	v: int
	open: bool
	switch sched.select(sched.on_recv(ch, &v, ok = &open)) {
	case 0: fmt.println("received; open:", open)
	}
}
```

```output
received; open: false
```

## `on_send`

```odin
on_send :: proc(c: Chan($T), v: T) -> Select_Case
```

A send of v for select.

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	ch := sched.make_chan(int, 1)
	switch sched.select(sched.on_send(ch, 9)) {
	case 0: fmt.println("sent", sched.recv(ch))
	}
}
```

```output
sent 9
```

## `select`

```odin
select :: proc(cases: ..Select_Case, loc := #caller_location) -> int
```

Waits until one case can proceed, runs it and returns its index.

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	nums := sched.make_chan(int, 1)
	words := sched.make_chan(string, 1)
	sched.send(words, "hi")
	n: int
	w: string
	switch sched.select(sched.on_recv(nums, &n), sched.on_recv(words, &w)) {
	case 0: fmt.println("number", n)
	case 1: fmt.println("word", w)
	}
}
```

```output
word hi
```

## `try_select`

```odin
try_select :: proc(cases: ..Select_Case, loc := #caller_location) -> int
```

Like select, but returns -1 at once when no case is ready.

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	ch := sched.make_chan(int)
	fmt.println(sched.try_select(sched.on_recv(ch)))    // -1: nothing ready
}
```

```output
-1
```

## `Wait_Group`

```odin
Wait_Group :: struct
```

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	wg: sched.Wait_Group
	for i in 0..<3 {
		sched.add(&wg)
		sched.go(proc[i, &wg]() {
			defer sched.done(&wg)
			sched.sleep(time.Duration(i) * time.Millisecond)
		})
	}
	sched.wait(&wg)
	fmt.println("all done")
}
```

```output
all done
```

## `add`

```odin
add :: proc(wg: ^Wait_Group, n := 1)
```

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	wg: sched.Wait_Group
	sched.add(&wg, 2)                 // two goroutines to wait for
	sched.go(proc[&wg]() { sched.done(&wg) })
	sched.go(proc[&wg]() { sched.done(&wg) })
	sched.wait(&wg)
	fmt.println("both finished")
}
```

```output
both finished
```

## `done`

```odin
done :: proc(wg: ^Wait_Group)
```

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	wg: sched.Wait_Group
	sched.add(&wg)
	sched.go(proc[&wg]() {
		defer sched.done(&wg)            // on every path out
		fmt.println("working")
	})
	sched.wait(&wg)
}
```

```output
working
```

## `wait`

```odin
wait :: proc(wg: ^Wait_Group, loc := #caller_location)
```

```vidar
main :: proc() {
	wg: sched.Wait_Group
	sched.wait(&wg)                       // nothing added: returns at once
	fmt.println("nothing to wait for")
}
```

```output
nothing to wait for
```
